facts.text: Glen Canyon Park began when Adolph Sutro bought 76 acres in the 1850s and called it 'Gum Tree Ranch' after planting blue gum eucalyptus.
The neighborhood grew from earthquake refugees in the late 19th century, blending historic homes with modern residences and small local businesses.
Glen Park’s name echoes its 1890s nickname 'Little Switzerland,' a nod to the windswept hills that resembled alpine scenery.
O'Shaughnessy Hollow, a 3.6‑acre rugged tract, sits just west of the park and is considered an extension of Glen Canyon Park.
The Glen Park Neighborhoods History Project, founded in 2014, documents the area’s diverse stories from the 1850s onward.
Glen Canyon Park’s Mission Zoo and extensive green space make it a key green lung for the surrounding neighborhoods.
